sources.note: Relayed from the NCLEX-RN case postop-fever-150-graves-meds-stopped, not re-read for this band; its note: Read 2026-11-17 through a summarizing fetch with quotes of the statpearls.com copy (NCBI refuses automated fetches): 'Fever of 104 F to 106 F with diaphoresis is a key presenting feature'; heart failure and atrial fibrillation; 'CNS involvement includes agitation, delirium, anxiety, psychosis, or coma'; nausea, vomiting, diarrhea and abdominal pain; precipitants include 'Abrupt discontinuation of antithyroid medicine', thyroid surgery and infections; mortality 'estimated to be 8 to 25%'; 'Thyroid storm is a true medical emergency that is fatal if left untreated'; supportive IV fluids, oxygen, cooling blankets and acetaminophen; 'The use of aspirin should be avoided due to its potential risk of increasing free thyroid hormone levels'; a beta-blocker for any suspected storm; 'Always administer thionamide before starting iodine solution'; treat the precipitant; admit to the ICU. The chapter's doses are not used.
